Modeling Monthly National Trend

crime_data %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    year_class = paste(class(Year), collapse = ","),
    month_class = paste(class(Month), collapse = ","),
    n_year_na = sum(is.na(Year)),
    n_month_na = sum(is.na(Month))
  )
##   n_rows year_class month_class n_year_na n_month_na
## 1 638454    integer   character         0          0
#converting month string to number
crime_clean <- crime_data %>%
  mutate(
    Month_num = case_when(
      Month == "January"   ~ 1,
      Month == "February"  ~ 2,
      Month == "March"     ~ 3,
      Month == "April"     ~ 4,
      Month == "May"       ~ 5,
      Month == "June"      ~ 6,
      Month == "July"      ~ 7,
      Month == "August"    ~ 8,
      Month == "September" ~ 9,
      Month == "October"   ~ 10,
      Month == "November"  ~ 11,
      Month == "December"  ~ 12
    ),
    ym = yearmonth(sprintf("%d-%02d", as.integer(Year), Month_num))
  )

crime_clean %>%
  count(ym) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ym, n)) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "National Monthly Crime Incidents",
       x ="Year",
       y = "Number of Incidents")

Creating Dataset for Heirarchical Models

city_month <- crime_clean %>%
  count(State, City, ym, name = "crime_count")

city_month %>%
  group_by(State, City) %>%
  summarise(avg_monthly = mean(crime_count)) %>%
  summary()
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'State'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
##     State               City            avg_monthly

##  Mode  :character   Mode  :character   Median :  1.162  
##                                        Mean   :  1.521  
##                                        3rd Qu.:  1.297  
##                                        Max.   :105.979

There’s a wide level of variation in the crime counts for different cities, so we may expect noisy bottom-level forecasts. Because there are so many cities, we model the top 5 cities within each state and then group everything else.

Restricting to top 5

top_cities <- city_month %>%
  group_by(State, City) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(crime_count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = total, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(State, City) %>%
  mutate(is_top = TRUE)

#relabeling cities not in top 5 as other
city5_other_month <- city_month %>%
  left_join(top_cities, by = c("State", "City")) %>%
  mutate(City_grp = if_else(is.na(is_top), "Other", City)) %>%
  group_by(State, City_grp, ym) %>%
  summarise(crime_count = sum(crime_count), .groups = "drop")

city5_other_month %>%
  distinct(State, City_grp) %>%
  count(State) %>%
  summary()
##     State                 n        
##  Length:51          Min.   :1.000  
##  Class :character   1st Qu.:6.000  
##  Mode  :character   Median :6.000  
##                     Mean   :5.784  
##                     3rd Qu.:6.000  
##                     Max.   :6.000

Creating State and National Totals and Converting to TS

state_month <- city5_other_month %>%
  group_by(State, ym) %>%
  summarise(crime_count = sum(crime_count), .groups = "drop")

national_month <- state_month %>%
  group_by(ym) %>%
  summarise(crime_count = sum(crime_count), .groups = "drop")

crime_ts <- city5_other_month %>%
  as_tsibble(key = c(State, City_grp), index = ym)

Investigating missing Data

expected_start <- yearmonth("1980 Apr")
expected_end   <- yearmonth("2014 Sep")
full_months <- as.integer(expected_end - expected_start) + 1

#restricting to expected time window of data
crime_win <- crime_clean %>%
  filter(ym >= expected_start, ym <= expected_end)

#monthly counts by city
city_month <- crime_win %>%
  count(State, City, ym, name = "crime_count")

#top 5 cities
top_cities <- city_month %>%
  group_by(State, City) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(crime_count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = total, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(State, City) %>%
  mutate(is_top = TRUE)

#relabeling as other
city5_other_month <- city_month %>%
  left_join(top_cities, by = c("State", "City")) %>%
  mutate(City_grp = if_else(is.na(is_top), "Other", City)) %>%
  group_by(State, City_grp, ym) %>%
  summarise(crime_count = sum(crime_count), .groups = "drop")

#coverage
coverage_citygrp <- city5_other_month %>%
  distinct(State, City_grp, ym) %>%
  group_by(State, City_grp) %>%
  summarise(
    start = min(ym),
    end   = max(ym),
    n_months_present = n(),
    coverage_pct = 100 * n_months_present / full_months,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(coverage_pct, State, City_grp)

coverage_citygrp

Converting to Time Series

crime_ts <- city5_other_month %>%
  as_tsibble(key = c(State, City_grp), index = ym)

#we fill any missing data with zeros only within each series
crime_ts_filled <- crime_ts %>%
  group_by_key() %>%
  fill_gaps(.full = FALSE, crime_count = 0)

is_regular(crime_ts_filled)
## [1] TRUE

Building the heirarchy

#aggregating the time series
crime_hier <- crime_ts_filled %>% aggregate_key(State / City_grp,
                                                crime_count = sum(crime_count))

crime_hier %>%
  distinct(State, City_grp) %>%
  count(State) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  head()
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
## Loading required namespace: crayon
##   State          n
##   <chr*>     <int>
## 1 Alabama        7
## 2 Alaska         7
## 3 Arizona        7
## 4 Arkansas       7
## 5 California     7
## 6 Colorado       7

Defining Train/Test Split

test_h <- 24

train <- crime_hier %>%
  group_by_key() %>%
  filter(row_number() <= n() - test_h) %>%
  ungroup()

test <- crime_hier %>%
  group_by_key() %>%
  filter(row_number() > n() - test_h) %>%
  ungroup()

Defining Base Forecasting Model

#defining base ETS forecasting model
fit_base <- train %>% model(base = ETS(crime_count))

Running 3 Base Models

#create reconciled versions of base model
fit_recon <- fit_base %>%
  reconcile(
    bottomup = bottom_up(base),
    topdown  = top_down(base),
    mint     = min_trace(base, method = "ols")
  )

Forecasting

fc_all <- fit_recon %>% forecast(h = test_h)

Accuracy

acc <- accuracy(fc_all, test)

acc_level <- acc %>%
  mutate(
    level = case_when(
      is_aggregated(State) & is_aggregated(City_grp) ~ "National",
      !is_aggregated(State) & is_aggregated(City_grp) ~ "State",
      TRUE ~ "City"
    )
  )

acc_level %>%
  group_by(.model, level) %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE = mean(RMSE),
    MAE  = mean(MAE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(level, RMSE)
## # A tibble: 12 × 4
##    .model   level      RMSE   MAE

Plotting National

fc_nat <- fc_all %>%
  filter(
    is_aggregated(State),
    is_aggregated(City_grp),
    .model != "base"   
  )

test_nat <- test %>%
  filter(is_aggregated(State), is_aggregated(City_grp))

fc_nat %>%
  autoplot(test_nat, level = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ .model, ncol = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "National Monthly Crime Forecasts by Reconciliation Method",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Crime Count"
  )

# Plotting State

rep_states <- c("California", "Michigan", "Vermont")

fc_state <- fc_all %>%
  filter(
    !is_aggregated(State),
    is_aggregated(City_grp),
    State %in% rep_states,
    .model != "base"
  )

test_state <- test %>%
  filter(
    !is_aggregated(State),
    is_aggregated(City_grp),
    State %in% rep_states
  )

fc_state %>%
  autoplot(test_state, level = NULL) +
  facet_grid(State ~ .model, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Representative State-Level Crime Forecasts",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Crime Count"
  )

Plotting City

rep_cities <- tibble::tribble(
  ~State,        ~City_grp,
  "California",  "Los Angeles",
  "Michigan",    "Wayne",
  "Vermont",     "Washington"
)

fc_city <- fc_all %>%
  semi_join(rep_cities, by = c("State", "City_grp")) %>%
  filter(
    !is_aggregated(State),
    !is_aggregated(City_grp),
    .model != "base"
  )

test_city <- test %>%
  semi_join(rep_cities, by = c("State", "City_grp")) %>%
  filter(
    !is_aggregated(State),
    !is_aggregated(City_grp)
  )

fc_city %>%
  autoplot(test_city, level = NULL) +
  facet_grid(paste(State, City_grp, sep = " - ") ~ .model, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Representative City-Level Crime Forecasts",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Crime Count"
  )
